title: 2-time Cy Young winner Skubal agrees to record 9-year, $450M US deal with Mets: reports
summary: Tarik Skubal, the two-time Cy Young Award winner who was the top free agent on this offseason's market, has a agreed to record $450 million US, nine-year contract with the New York Mets, a person…

image.caption: The New York Mets and ace pitcher Tarik Skubal have agreed to a record-setting 9-year, $450M US deal on Sunday, according to multiple reports. (Patrick McDermott/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Tarik Skubal, the two-time Cy Young Award winner who was the top free agent on this offseason's market, has a agreed to record $450 million US, nine-year contract with the New York Mets, a person familiar the negotiations told The Associated Press on Sunday.
Blue Jays were reportedly among teams who met with 30-year-old ace

Tarik Skubal, the two-time Cy Young Award winner who was this offseason's top free agent, has agreed to a record $450 million US, nine-year contract with the New York Mets, a person familiar with the negotiations told The Associated Press on Sunday.
The person spoke on condition of anonymity because the agreement was subject to a successful physical.

Skubal's deal, averaging $50 million annually, is the largest for a pitcher, topping Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million, 12-year contract with the Los Angeles Dodgers that started in 2024. The previous high for a pitcher's average annual value was $43.33 million for Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander.
It's the fourth largest deal among all baseball players, trailing Juan Soto's $765 million, Shohei Ohtani's $700 million and Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s $500 million.
The Toronto Blue Jays were among multiple teams reported to have met with Skubal prior to agreeing to join the Mets.

Skubal's agreement includes a full no-trade clause and a $45 million signing bonus that is shielded from the management lockout that threatens the 2027 season, the person said. It includes $30 million in deferred payments from 2036-45.

He joins a Mets team that finished last in the NL East at 74-88 despite owner Steve Cohen bankrolling baseball's highest payroll on opening day at roughly $352 million. New York's starters had a 4.47 ERA, ranking 23rd in the majors. Skubal will top a rotation featuring youngsters Nolan McLean and Christian Scott, with veterans Sean Manaea and Kodai Senga also under contract.

Skubal had plans to meet with at least six teams this month, including the Mets, Los Angeles Dodgers and San Diego Padres. His deal comes about a week before MLB owners are expected to lock out the players in a labor fight centreing on management's push for a salary cap. MLB has proposed a hard cap of $258.2 million for 2028. Skubal and Soto alone would account for nearly 40 per cent of that cap.
A two-time All-Star left-hander who turned 30 on Nov. 20, Skubal is 43-17 with a 2.42 ERA in 88 starts over the last four seasons, striking out 655 and walking 95 in 546 innings.
Skubal had a $32 million salary this year after winning a record amount in salary arbitration.

Tigers pitcher Tarik Skubal to have elbow surgery to remove loose bodies

blocks.text: Skubal was 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA in 26 starts this year for Detroit and the Los Angeles Dodgers, who acquired him on Aug. 2 for three prospects: right-handers River Ryan and Brady Smith, and outfielder Zyhir Hope. Skubal didn't pitch for the Tigers between April 29 and June 13 because of surgery to remove a loose body in his pitching elbow. Dodgers head team physician Dr. Neal ElAttrache used a NanoNeedle scope 2.0 to perform the procedure, designed to speed recovery.

Skubal was 1-1 with a 2.45 ERA in a pair of postseason starts for the Dodgers. He beat Atlanta in a Division Series opener and lost Game 1 of the NL League Championship Series against Milwaukee, allowing two runs over five innings in a 2-1 defeat. The Brewers went on to sweep the two-time defending World Series champions.

He averaged 96.8 mph with his four-seam fastball this year, down from 97.6 mph in 2025, when he won his second straight AL Cy Young Award. He threw 38 per cent four-seamers this year, 25.6 per cent changeups, 17.5 per cent sinkers, 13.9 per cent sliders and 5 per cent curveballs.
Skubal is 66-44 with a 3.02 ERA in 160 starts and three relief appearances over seven major league seasons with 1,075 strikeouts over 925 1/3 innings.
